title: Parking Brake Cable Adjustment — SVT Performance Package
introduction:
This adjustment applies to the Mustang with the SVT Performance Package and manual transmission. The parking-brake lever stays at its first click while the cable adjustment nut is tightened underneath the vehicle.

I let the rear wheels grade the adjustment: they should turn with resistance at that lever position, then spin freely when the brake is released. Think of the cable as a drawstring—the useful setting comes from how it pulls, so the wheel checks decide when to stop tightening.

requirements.category: Prevent unexpected starting and protect yourself

items.name: Secure the car and control ignition
items.detail: Begin on hard, level ground with the parking brake applied and wheels chocked. Keep the engine stopped throughout. Disable remote start, if equipped, through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before dismantling. Otherwise the vehicle could start unexpectedly and cause serious injury or death. If the menu needs power, keep the valid key inside; from confirmed OFF press and release START/STOP without either pedal to select engine-off ON. If already ON with the engine stopped, retain ON. After the setting change, return ON to OFF without pressing a pedal; if already OFF, leave OFF. From the ground-accessible cabin, select Neutral on the manual transmission while the parking brake and chocks prevent movement. With ignition OFF, remove the key before service. Keep the parking brake applied until the securely supported transition to the first-click setting described below.

items.name: Wear protective equipment
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection while servicing the vehicle, and protective gloves when handling pointed or sharp-edged parts. Failure to use the specified protection may result in serious personal injury. Review the applicable [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189) before starting.

requirements.category: Prepare the hoist and lifting points

items.name: Plan ground-level access to the lever
items.detail: Use a securely supported working height that allows underside access and lets a helper reach the parking-brake lever while standing on the floor beside the open door. Nobody climbs into the raised car. If the hoist cannot provide both safe access and this lever reach, arrange suitable workshop access before starting. Keep all wheels fully clear of the ground before reducing or releasing the parking brake. Do not run the engine for these hand-rotation checks.

items.name: Confirm capacity and arm placement
items.detail: Use a hoist with sufficient capacity for the vehicle, including cargo and modifications. Locate the stamped triangles marking the lifting points along the side sills, behind the front wheels and ahead of the rear wheels. Position the lift arms at those points using [Jacking and Lifting - Overview](#/document/G1663631). Lifting elsewhere can let the vehicle shift or fall, causing serious personal injury. Incorrect hoist arm placement can cause unintended movement, serious personal injury or death.

items.name: Check clearance before lifting
items.detail: Keep the hoist adapters and forks clear of the suspension, exhaust, steering linkage, mounting brackets and stabilizer mounting brackets, if equipped. Avoid contact that could damage the axle or rear cover. The adjustment itself requires the rear wheels to be off the ground for the rotation checks.

items.name: Use proper vehicle support
items.detail: Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack; it may lower unexpectedly and cause serious personal injury. A jack-raised vehicle requires floor stands. The vehicle's emergency jack is for changing a deflated tire and must not be used to hoist the vehicle for this adjustment. Never apply jack pressure to either bumper, because the bumper covers will be damaged.

items.name: Review the brake safety reference
items.detail: Before beginning, review [Brake and Clutch Systems Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693183). This cable adjustment does not require opening the hydraulic system or removing friction components.

items.name: Avoid exposure to friction dust
items.detail: If friction-component dust is encountered, do not breathe it or use compressed air to blow it from friction components or storage containers. Remove dust using government-approved techniques. Exposure can cause cancer or lung disease, skin, eye and respiratory irritation, allergic reactions or other chronic health effects, and may result in serious personal injury. Seek medical attention or advice if irritation persists.

edits.text: Place the transmission in NEUTRAL and position the vehicle on a hoist. Refer to [Jacking and Lifting - Overview](#/document/G1663631) (100-02 Jacking and Lifting, Description and Operation).
edits.why: The rear wheels must be available for rotation checks during adjustment. Position the hoist at the marked body lifting points before raising the vehicle. Retain the parking brake and wheel chocks while selecting service Neutral on the manual transmission. Establish secure hoist support with all wheels clear before reducing the lever setting; the parking brake must not be the only thing preventing movement.

edits.text: Pull the parking-brake lever up to its first click/position.
edits.why: The lever drawing identifies the initial ratchet position. Keep this setting while adjusting the cables underneath; it establishes the lever position at which wheel resistance is checked. With all wheels clear and the vehicle securely supported, the floor-standing helper can set this position: press and hold the button at the end of the lever, pull the lever up slightly and lower it fully, release the button, then pull it to its first click. Keep hands and tools clear of the brake mechanisms while the lever moves. Nobody enters the raised cabin.

edits.text: NOTICE: Check rear-wheel rotation frequently while tightening the parking brake cables to prevent overtightening. Tighten only until the rear wheels no longer spin freely and have resistance. Make sure the rear wheels are not locked.
edits.why: Resistance is the adjustment target at this lever position. A wheel that cannot turn has gone beyond that target.

edits.text: Raise the vehicle and tighten the parking brake cable adjustment nut, checking rear-wheel rotation frequently until the following conditions are met.
edits.why: The underbody drawing highlights the nut on the threaded rod at the cable equalizer, where the cable runs meet. I use that location to identify the adjuster, then judge the setting by the wheel behavior below.

edits.text: The rear wheels turn with resistance instead of spinning freely.
edits.why: This is the required wheel behavior with the lever still at its initial click.

edits.text: The rear wheels remain able to turn; they are not locked.
edits.why: Both conditions must be satisfied together. Resistance alone is insufficient if the wheels have become locked.

edits.text: Lower the vehicle on the hoist while keeping the wheels off the ground and the suspension in the full rebound position. Release the parking brake, then confirm that both rear wheels spin freely.
edits.why:
Full rebound means the wheels remain hanging with the suspension extended, rather than carrying the vehicle's weight. This final check confirms that the adjustment allows the brake to release. If either rear wheel still has resistance, the required release check has not passed. Clear tools and everyone from underneath before lowering to the securely supported check height; keep every wheel off the ground. The floor-standing helper releases the lever by pressing and holding its end button, pulling it up slightly and lowering it. Keep hands clear during lever movement, then check both rear wheels by hand. If either fails to turn freely, stop and resolve the failed adjustment before driving.

After the checks, remove tools and clear everyone underneath. Have the floor-standing helper pull the handle up as far as possible to fully apply the parking brake before lowering onto the tires, restoring wheel chocks as the tires meet the ground. Once fully grounded with the parking brake applied and chocks in place, hold the clutch pedal down and select first gear. Finish with the engine stopped, ignition OFF and key outside, all tools accounted for and hoist arms clear.

editorialRevision.scope: Known ignition states, manual Neutral/first gear, secure hoist/helper transitions and actual parking lever controls. Original technical action texts and wheel criteria unchanged; operational safety transitions are editorial clarification.
